claim: SF's iconic visitor foods/drinks include Irish coffee at Buena Vista Cafe (up to 2,000 daily), Boudin sourdough since 1849, Mission burritos at El Farolito and Taqueria La Cumbre, Dungeness crab and cioppino at Fisherman's Wharf, and Chinatown dim sum.
quote: Irish Coffee — hot coffee, Irish whiskey and whipped cream served at Buena Vista Cafe; Boudin Sourdough operating since 1849; Mission Burrito at El Farolito and Taqueria La Cumbre; seafood at Fog Harbor Fish House; Dim Sum found throughout Chinatown

claim: Dungeness crab season runs November to June and peaks January through March, and cioppino is a hearty seafood stew created in SF in the early 1900s from the city's Italian-American roots.
quote: Crab season runs November to June, peaking January–March. Cioppino, a hearty seafood stew that showcases the city's Italian-American roots, created in the early 1900s.

claim: San Francisco has 30 Michelin-starred restaurants in 2026: three with three stars (Benu, Quince, Atelier Crenn), six with two stars (including Lazy Bear), and 21 with one star (Nari, Kin Khao, State Bird Provisions, Gary Danko).
quote: There are three restaurants in San Francisco with three Michelin stars, six restaurants with two stars and 21 restaurants with a single Michelin star.

claim: Benu became SF's first three-Michelin-star restaurant in 2014 under chef Corey Lee, and Atelier Crenn's Dominique Crenn was the first female chef in the US to earn three Michelin stars with a pescatarian tasting menu.
quote: Benu... became San Francisco's first to earn three Michelin stars in 2014. Chef Dominique Crenn made history as the first female chef in the United States to earn three Michelin stars. Her pescatarian tasting menu...

claim: The Ferry Building Marketplace houses nearly 50 local artisan food merchants and eateries, while the adjacent Ferry Plaza Farmers Market (run by nonprofit Foodwise since 1993) draws 100+ vendors on Saturdays, also operating Tuesday and Thursday.
quote: nearly 50 local artisan food merchants, restaurants and small eateries... Since 1993, the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market... With over 100+ vendors, the Saturday market is held both in front of the Ferry Building... Tuesday 10am-2pm, Thursday 10am-2pm, Saturday 8am-2pm

claim: SF's specialty-coffee landmarks include Sightglass (warehouse roastery with an affogato bar), Four Barrel (vintage German roaster, no wifi), Andytown's Snowy Plover (espresso, brown-sugar syrup and San Pellegrino over ice), and Wrecking Ball, whose owner coined 'third-wave coffee.'
quote: Andytown... famous for the Snowy Plover drink: San Pellegrino, brown-sugar syrup and two shots of espresso over ice finished with whipped cream. Wrecking Ball... Owner Trish Rothgeb coined the term 'third-wave coffee.'

claim: San Francisco helped define modern specialty coffee, with Blue Bottle, Sightglass, Ritual, and Four Barrel building their reputations locally; the Mission has the highest density of coffee shops.
quote: San Francisco helped define modern specialty coffee—Blue Bottle started across the bay, and Sightglass, Ritual, and Four Barrel all built their reputations here. Mission has the highest density of coffee shops

claim: Pacific Cocktail Haven, near Union Square, ranks on North America's 50 Best Bars with a multi-page menu leaning on Asian-Pacific ingredients like tea, guava and calamansi, and takes no reservations.
quote: a lively cocktail bar just a few blocks from Union Square... cocktails inspired by Asian Pacific flavors... leaning towards Asian Pacific ingredients such as tea, guava and calamansi. No reservations are accepted

claim: Standout SF cocktail bars include Smuggler's Cove (immersive nautical rum bar with a global rum selection) and Trick Dog in the Mission (creative seasonal themed cocktail menus).
quote: Smuggler's Cove is a mystical escape transporting guests to a world of rum... an impressive array of rums from around the globe. Trick Dog is a ridiculously popular bar in the Mission that serves creative cocktails... seasonal, themed menu.

claim: Tartine Bakery in the Mission is a James Beard-winning SF institution opened around 2002 whose country sourdough loaf (about $14.75) is widely regarded as the city's best.
quote: twenty years after opening, Tartine still makes the best sourdough in San Francisco... The country loaf costs $14.75 and is golden brown on the outside, soft and gummy on the inside... Tartine has earned a James Beard Award
